findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed carrots stored below raw fish in the prep cooler. CORRECTED- carrots were voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Ensure ready to eat food are always stored ABOVE raw foods to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: PIC began to don gloves after handling a cellphone without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the behavior and reminded PIC to wash hands, which they did, then donned gloves to continue work. Ensure employees wash hands after any task that may have contaminated them and before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink was observed blocked by a roll of plastic wrap upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- PIC moved the plastic wrap so the handsink is accessible. Keep handsinks clear and accessible at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: There is no ambient thermometer present inside of the bottom of the prep cooler. Ensure thermometers are provided inside all cold holding units (in addition to any digital thermometers that may be built in to the units).
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment: A sealed package of ROP tuna was observed thawed in the bottom of the sushi prep cooler. The package had written instructions to remove from packaging before thawing. Upon request, PIC cut the package and removed the thawed fish. Ensure ROP fish is thawed according to the supplier’s instructions.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13 (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient thermometer was present inside of the bottom of the prep cooler. Ensure thermometers are provided inside all cold holding units (in addition to any digital thermometers that may be built in to the units).
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
One of the two employees present has not completed food handler training. Ensure all employees who handle food or wash dishes complete food handler training within 30 days of hire. Keep food handler certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee began to don gloves after handling their phone without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the employee, who then washed hands and donned gloves. Wash hands before donning gloves and after any activity that may have contaminated hands.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not setup for use. PIC provided quat solution during inspection. Ensure sanitizer solution is setup and available for use prior to beginning food preparation and packaging. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Freshly prepared sushi products were placed directly in the display case and were not properly cooled to 41F/below in the walk-in freezer or walk-in cooler as required by the FujiSan HACCP plan. Internal temperatures were observed above 50F for products placed in the display case after morning prep. Spicy California rolls that were getting packaged in the prep room were observed with internal temperatures of 57F-61F. All products prepared as of this morning were taken to the walk-in freezer to allow for proper chilling before being placed back in the display case. 
The pH for sushi rice prepared this morning was not documented in the Managers Red Book (daily HACCP documentation log). PIC at time of inspection stated the pH meter was calibrated and used this morning to verify proper pH of rice. When asked to demonstrate calibration of pH meter and show pH of sushi rice, the pH meter would not stabilize at 4.0 for buffer solution. PIC stated the pH meter currently in use is new, and PIC was unsure as to what might be wrong with it. Inspector will return on 2/1/22 when manager is back from training to verify proper function of pH meter.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC changed gloves without washing hands. Handwashing between glove changes was discussed. PIC was observed washing hands as needed for remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed prior to donning gloves and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Ice water used for calibration of food thermometer was discarded in the handwashing sink. Proper use of handwashing sink was discussed. Ensure the handwashing sink if not used as a dump sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) 1. PIC handled wallet with gloved hands when getting out their manager certification card. Gloves were not removed prior to approaching prep area to continue food handling. PIC was advised on proper glove use. Gloves were discarded and hands washed prior to PIC putting on a new pair of gloves. 
2. The other person helping with prep was observed touching their face mask with gloved hands. PIC was advised to ensure gloves are changed between tasks and after face masks are touched or adjusted. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Freshly prepared sushi products placed directly in the display case had internal temperatures above 50F. California rolls were observed at 57F. All products prepared this morning were moved to the walk-in freezer to quickly chill to proper temperature. Packaged products were moved back to the display case after reaching internal temperatures of 30F-33F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not setup for use. PIC provided quat solution during inspection. Ensure sanitizer solution is setup and available for use prior to beginning food preparation and packaging. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Worker assisting PIC at time of inspection did not have a food handler certification. The need for certification was discussed. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Facility manager has been documenting calibration of the food thermometer daily for the past 2 weeks but confirmed the food thermometer was not getting checked as required by company HACCP plan. Manager was unsure where to get ice for calibration. Manager got ice from the cafe at the request of inspector and was able to confirm calibration at 32F during inspection. Manager was advised to follow the FujiSan HACCP requirements and make sure calibration of the food thermometer occurs daily along with calibration of the pH meter prior to use. Documentation should not be made otherwise if calibration hasn’t occurred as that is falsifying documents. 
Manager has also been documenting time for acidified rice at 6am when calibration of pH meter is being documented at 7am. Manager confirmed the time in the log was when the rice finished cooking prior to adding rice vinegar after calibration of the pH meter. Time when rice is acidified needs to be documented. Manager stated he understood and will change his practice to allow for proper documentation.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution in sanitizer-bucket was at 100ppm. Solution was prepared upon arrival of manager early this morning. Fresh sanitizer solution was prepared at 200ppm. Manager was advised to change the solution throughout operations daily as needed based on use.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged Ahi tuna steaks and salmon were observed in the walkin cooler. Manager stated the packages are not opened until product is needed and noted the products in question would be used within the next two days. Directions on the packaging states to open the package and thaw under refrigeration immediately before use. Manager was advised on proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish. Ensure vacuum packaged frozen fish are removed from the package and thawed in a covered pan under refrigeration or at minimum the packaging is opened to eliminate the reduced oxygen environment. Follow the directions on packaging when thawing any portions of vacuum packaged fish. **See general comments for additional information**
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, its thawing using cold running water as specified in the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Thawed portions of vacuum packaged Ahi tuna steaks were observed in the walkin cooler. Directions on the packaging states to open the package and thaw under refrigeration immediately before use. PIC was advised on proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish. Ensure vacuum packaged frozen fish are removed from the package and thawed in a covered pan under refrigeration or at minimum the packaging is opened to eliminate the reduced oxygen environment. Follow the directions on packaging when thawing any portions of vacuum packaged fish.
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, its thawing using cold running water as specified in the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 PIC and assistant were in the process of preparing crab rolls upon arrival of inspector. Preparation ceased, and PIC was advised the prep/package process could be finished so items could be placed in the walkin freezer for chilling prior to continuing with inspection. PIC indicated the product was ok sitting out. Several minutes later the internal temperature was observed at 50F. Inspector asked PIC to put crab rolls away in cold holding until prep/package process could be quickly and safely completed. Crab rolls were placed in a covered pan in the walkin cooler for holding. Chilled pans of crab and spicy crab meat had surface temperatures at 42F-43F and internal tempreratures of 39F and were allowed to remain out for use. PIC was advised to monitor temperatures and return pans of crab and other foods to the walkin cooler if internal temperatures are above 41F.
NOTE: When a significant interruption occurs, ensure products are immediately placed back in cold holding and not left in the prep room. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged fish was observed in the walkin cooler thawing for use. Directions on the packaging states to remove from package and thaw under refrigeration. PIC was advised on proper thawing of vacuum packaged fish. Ensure vacuum packaged frozen fish are removed from the package and thawed in a covered pan under refrigeration.
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration or prior to, or immediately upon completion of, its thawing using cold running water as specified in the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Knife was observed in sanitizer solution located in the sani-bucket. Knife was used wtih sticky rice and placed in the bucket for storage between uses. PIC stated the knife is wiped down with a fresh wiping cloth prior to use. PIC was advised to cease the practice and to leave the knife out in the prep area on a clean surface between uses. Knife may be wiped with a sanitizer solution between uses during prep and needs to be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use along with all preparation surfaces. PIC removed the knife and placed it at the 3 part sink for ware washing.  
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utnesils shall be stored on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensils and the food-contact  surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11 of the 2017 FDA Food Code.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Block of cream cheese was open and without a date mark. PIC noted it was opened on the Saturday prior. Date mark of 11/23 was provided. Ensure all ready to eat, TCS foods are properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days or the time frame required by corporate documentation.
Ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be clearly dated after preparation (foods made on-site) or after original packaging is opened (commercially processed foods) and shall be used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration. The day of preparation and/or the original packaging is opened shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 PIC has a different person helping at the facility since the last inspection. That person does not have a food handler certification on file. PIC was advised the new worker, even if only helping during the holiday season, needs to complete the online food handler training. A copy of the certification needs to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 PIC was not documenting information in the daily log book as required by the company HACCP plan. When asked why no information was documented for rice preparation, calibration of tools (pH meter and food thermometer), and other required documentation, the PIC stated she remembers information and writes it down at the end of the day. PIC was advised this information must be written down as tasks are completed and she should not be relying on memory alone. Also, as tasks occur if issues arise, corrective actions need to be accurately documented.
Sushi rice was prepared around 12pm based on information provided, but the time was not documented anywhere. Sushi rice is required to be used or discarded within 6hrs of preparation and must have a pH of 4.1 or below per the company standard. Due to lack of documentation, PIC was asked to calibrate the pH meter and check the pH of the rice during inspection. Sushi rice was observed with a pH of 4.2. When PIC was advised to add more vinegar to lower the acidity, she seemed confused and asked if more rice needs to be added to change the pH. The pH was lowered by adding more vinegar and was observed with a pH of 4.0 after corrective action was taken. PIC was advised to follow the steps in the directions provided in the HACCP plan every day to ensure proper pH of sushi rice. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC returned to sushi prep area after being in another part of the store and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to handle pans of various food items. Gloves were removed and hands were washed upon request of inspector.
The other worker arrived later during the inspection and was preparing to put on gloves without first washing hands. PIC advised worker to wash his hands before putting on gloves for prep. Worker washed his hands prior to putting on gloves upon request of PIC.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed any time hands may have been contaminated, upon entering the work area, and before putting on gloves/between glove changes.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Various food items that were out in the refrigerated prep room were placed in the walkin cooler upon arrival of inspector. PIC noted the foods were out in the prep room for ~3hrs. Raw fish was observed at 43F-44F. A few items were observed at 45F. Spicy crab meat was observed at 47F. The temperature of spicy crab meat was observed at 40F approximately 30 minutes later after storage in the walkin cooler. PIC was advised that foods requiring time/temperature control for safety need to be monitored frequently during hours of use in the prep room and rotated back in the walkin cooler for storage prior to reaching temperatures above 45F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Food additives: approved and properly used
findings.citation_text:
3-302.14 Sushi rice was observed with a pH of 4.2 Sushi rice prepared with vinegar for the purposes of acidification must be at 4.1 or below. More vinegar was added to the sushi rice, and the pH was observed at 4.0. 
Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from the addition of unsafe levels of approved food additives.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12 Squeeze bottles of various sauces were observed without labels or had old labels that indicated they were past the time frame for use. All sauces were labeled during the inspection. Mayonnaise and spicy mayo have a 14 day shelf life once opened and prepared. All other sauces have a 30 day shelf life once opened for use. PIC was advised to maintain proper labels. Remove old labels prior to cleaning and sanitizing bottles between uses to avoid confusion on the use by date. 
Except for containers holding food that can be readily and unmistakably recognized, working containers holding food or food ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the food establishment, such as sauces, shall be identified with the common name of the food.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.citation_text:
6-501.18 Mold buildup was observed in the basin and drain of the handsink in the refrigerated prep room. Cleaning of the handsink and related fixtures was discussed. 
Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Employee that does not have a CFM was said to have a food handler certification. A copy of the certification was not available for viewing. PIC was advised to provide a copy of the food handler certification for the other worker. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to have a food handler certification, and copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Crab meat observed in walkin cooler had a prep date of 3/20 and use by date of 3/28. Operator stated the product is good for 8 days and stated proper documentation was available. Operator was advised to count day of preparation as Day 1, which would mean the use by date would be 3/27 instead of 3/28. Label was changed to reflect proper time frame for service. 

Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat time/temperature control for safety foods shall be clearly marked, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Raw and cooked fish and seafood products and sauces in the prep/holding room (shared with the deli) had internal temperatures ranging from 46°F-48°F. Several products were out and in use since 7a and 9a based on information provided. All items in question were discarded. Two roll carts containing prepared portions of sushi and ingredients for making sushi were moved to the walkin cooler, which was holding below 40°F.

Cold foods that require time/temperature for safety shall be maintained at 41°F/below at all times during storage, display, and service. NOTE: Sushi fish must be maintained at colder temperatures - follow the instructions of Fujisan HACCP plan and see binder on-site for details.

Sushi rice was observed with a pH of 4.6. According to the directions of the Fujisan manual the pH must be at 4.1. Manager stated the rice was still hot, but the rice had surface and internal temperatures of 74°F and 88°F respectively. The manager was advised the rice was not hot. Rice was cooked ~1.5hrs prior. The pH meter was calibrated per the instructions in the HACCP plan, and more vinegar was added to the rice. The pH was then observed at 4.4. Manager was advised to add more vinegar until the rice reaches proper pH.

Every batch of rice is to be checked for proper pH of 4.1, and the pH meter is to be calibrated every time it is used according to the Fujisan manual. Each batch of rice has a maximum hold/use time of 6hrs. Follow the directions and do this process properly to ensure rice will not support the growth of bacteria. Maintain sushi rice at a pH of 4.1 and discard within 6hrs.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 -  Certified food manager was gone for a break upon arrival of inspector. Employee on-site used his cell phone to call the manager. Employee then put on his chef coat and began moving items around on a cart without first washing his hands. Employee was advised to wash his hands.
Upon arrival the manager was advised on proper handwashing and to wash hands upon entering the prep area and after touching anything unrelated to food handling/preparation.

Hands shall be properly washed any time they may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Half empty bottle of water was observed on the bottom shelf of the prep table. It was assumed to be the other employee's personal beverage. Water was discarded during the inspection.

Employees shall consume food and beverage only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Items were being cleaned and sanitized at the 3 part sink but the proper contact time was not occurring. Manager used soap solution dispensed directly from the chemical hose. Then rinsed items with water from the sprayer prior to rinsing with sanitizer solution dispensed directly from the chemical hose. Proper manual ware washing was discussed. Educational handout was provided.

Three sinks shall be provided and used for proper ware washing. Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).
NOTE: all equipment needs to be submerged in sanitizer solution for a minimum of 60 seconds prior to being removed for air drying.
